arxiv-2012-02542.title: Crop Classification under Varying Cloud Cover with Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
arxiv-2012-02542.creator: Nando Metzger*, Mehmet Ozgur Turkoglu*, Stefano D’Aronco, Jan Dirk Wegner, Konrad Schindler
arxiv-2012-02542.description: Abstract Optical satellite sensors cannot see the Earth’s surface through clouds. Despite the periodic revisit cycle, image sequences acquired by Earth observation satellites are therefore irregularly sampled in time. State-of-the-art methods for crop classification (and other time series analysis tasks) rely on techniques that implicitly assume regular temporal spacing between observations, such as recurrent neural networks (RNNs).

arxiv-2102-01790.title: Couplings of the Random-Walk Metropolis algorithm
arxiv-2102-01790.creator: John O’Leary
arxiv-2102-01790.description: Abstract Couplings play a central role in contemporary Markov chain Monte Carlo methods and in the analysis of their convergence to stationarity. In most cases, a coupling must induce relatively fast meeting between chains to ensure good performance. In this paper we fix attention on the random walk Metropolis algorithm and examine a range of coupling design choices.

arxiv-2103-01690.title: Towards holographic flat bands
arxiv-2103-01690.creator: Nicolás Grandi, Vladimir Juričić, Ignacio Salazar Landea, Rodrigo Soto-Garrido
arxiv-2103-01690.description: Abstract Motivated by the phenomenology in the condensed-matter flat-band Dirac systems, we here construct a holographic model that imprints the symmetry breaking pattern of a rather simple Dirac fermion model at zero chemical potential.In the bulk we explicitly include the backreaction to the corresponding Lifshitz geometry and compute the dynamical critical exponent.

arxiv-2107-14623.title: Phonon anomalies associated with spin reorientation in the Kagome ferromagnet Fe 3 Sn 2
arxiv-2107-14623.description: Abstract Polarization- and temperature-dependent Raman data along with theoretical simulations are presented for the Kagome ferromagnet Fe 3 Sn 2 . Eight out of nine expected phonon modes were identified. The experimental energies compare well with those from the simulations. The analysis of the line widths indicates relatively strong phonon-phonon coupling in the range 0.1 to 1.

arxiv-2206-13754.title: DistSPECTRL: Distributing Specifications in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Systems
arxiv-2206-13754.creator: Joe Eappen (✉), Suresh Jagannathan
arxiv-2206-13754.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Joe Eappen (✉), Suresh Jagannathan. While notable progress has been made in specifying and learning objectives for general cyber-physical systems, applying these methods to distributed multi-agent systems still pose significant challenges. Among these are the need to (a) craft specification primitives that allow expression and interplay of both local and global objectives, (b) tame explosion in the state and action spaces to enable effective learning, and (c) minimize coordination frequency and the set of engaged participants for global objectives.

arxiv-2207-07044.title: A rapidly mixing Markov chain from any gapped quantum many-body system
arxiv-2207-07044.creator: Sergey Bravyi, Giuseppe Carleo, David Gosset, Yinchen Liu
arxiv-2207-07044.description: Abstract We consider the computational task of sampling a bit string x x from a distribution π ⁡ ( x ) = | ⟨ x | ψ ⟩ | 2 \pi(x)=|\langle x|\psi\rangle|^{2} , where ψ \psi is the unique ground state of a local Hamiltonian H H .

arxiv-2302-04603.title: Contestable Camera Cars: A Speculative Design Exploration of Public AI That Is Open and Responsive to Dispute DOI: 10.1145/3544548.3580984 Conference: Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 23–28, 2023; Hamburg, Germany Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Confere
arxiv-2302-04603.creator: Kars Alfrink, Ianus Keller, Neelke Doorn, Gerd Kortuem
arxiv-2302-04603.description: Abstract . Local governments increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) for automated decision-making. Contestability, making systems responsive to dispute, is a way to ensure they respect human rights to autonomy and dignity. We investigate the design of public urban AI systems for contestability through the example of camera cars: human-driven vehicles equipped with image sensors.

arxiv-2404-00512.title: Teleportation two-qubit state by using two different protocols
arxiv-2404-00512.creator: K. El anouz, A. El Allati, N. Metwally
arxiv-2404-00512.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by K. El anouz, A. El Allati, N. Metwally. In this contribution, two versions of teleportation protocol are considered, based on either using a single or two copies of entangled atom-field state, respectively. It is shown that, by using the first version, the fidelity of the teleported state as well as the amount of quantum Fisher information, that contains in the teleported state, are much better than using the second version.

arxiv-2409-09213.title: ReCLAP: Improving Zero Shot Audio Classification by Describing Sounds
arxiv-2409-09213.creator: Sreyan Ghosh ♠ Sonal Kumar ♠ ​ \vardiamondsuit {}^{\spadesuit\vardiamondsuit} Chandra Kiran Reddy Evuru \vardiamondsuit {}^{\vardiamondsuit} Oriol Nieto \vardiamondsuit {}^{\vardiamondsuit} Ramani Duraiswami \vardiamondsuit {}^{\vardiamondsuit} Dinesh Manocha \vardiamondsuit {}^{\vardiamondsuit}
arxiv-2409-09213.description: Abstract Open-vocabulary audio-language models, like CLAP [ 1 ] , offer a promising approach for zero-shot audio classification (ZSAC) by enabling classification with any arbitrary set of categories specified with natural language prompts. In this paper, we propose a simple but effective method to improve ZSAC with CLAP.

arxiv-2501-02855.title: Synthetic Fungi Datasets: A Time-Aligned Approach
arxiv-2501-02855.creator: Anju Rani, Daniel O. Arroyo, Petar Durdevic
arxiv-2501-02855.description: Abstract Fungi undergo dynamic morphological transformations throughout their lifecycle, forming intricate networks as they transition from spores to mature mycelium structures. To support the study of these time-dependent processes, we present a synthetic, time-aligned image dataset that models key stages of fungal growth.

arxiv-2503-07021.title: Learning energy-based models by self-normalising the likelihood
arxiv-2503-07021.creator: Hugo Senetaire, Paul Jeha, Pierre-Alexandre Mattei, Jes Frellsen
arxiv-2503-07021.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hugo Senetaire, Paul Jeha, Pierre-Alexandre Mattei, Jes Frellsen. Training an energy-based model (EBM) with maximum likelihood is challenging due to the intractable normalisation constant. Traditional methods rely on expensive Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling to estimate the gradient of logartihm of the normalisation constant. We propose a novel objective called self-normalised log-likelihood (SNL) that introduces a single additional learnable parameter representing the normalisation constant compared to the regular log-likelihood.

arxiv-2509-05432.title: Explicit Generators for the Unit Group of the Burnside ring
arxiv-2509-05432.creator: Ziad Ghanem
arxiv-2509-05432.description: Abstract . To the best of our knowledge, there is no explicit, constructive description of the generating set for the unit group A ​ ( G ) × A(G)^{\times} of the Burnside ring associated with a finite group G G .

arxiv-2509-12090.title: End-to-End 4D Heart Mesh Recovery Across Full-Stack and Sparse Cardiac MRI
arxiv-2509-12090.creator: Yihong Chen, Jiancheng Yang, Deniz Sayin Mercadier, Hieu Le, Juerg Schwitter, Pascal Fua
arxiv-2509-12090.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yihong Chen, Jiancheng Yang, Deniz Sayin Mercadier, Hieu Le, Juerg Schwitter, Pascal Fua. Reconstructing cardiac motion from cine CMR sequences is critical for diagnosis, prediction, and intervention. Existing methods rely on complete CMR stacks to infer full heart motion, limiting their utility in intra-procedural scenarios where only sparse observations are available. We present TetHeart , the first end-to-end framework that unifies full 4D multi-structure heart mesh recovery from both offline full-stack acquisitions and intra-procedural sparse-slice observations.

arxiv-2602-22707.title: SCOPE: Skeleton Graph-Based Computation-Efficient Framework for Autonomous UAV Exploration Thanks: This paper was supported by the Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant 62371269, Shenzhen Science and Technology Program ZDCYKCX20250901094203005, Shenzhen Low-Altitude Airspace Strategic Prog

arxiv-2602-22707.description: Abstract Autonomous exploration in unknown environments is key for mobile robots, helping them perceive, map, and make decisions in complex areas. However, current methods often rely on frequent global optimization, suffering from high computational latency and trajectory oscillation, especially on resource-constrained edge devices.

europmc-pmc4739513.title: Spectrally resolved fast transient brain states in electrophysiological data.
europmc-pmc4739513.creator: Vidaurre D, Quinn AJ, Baker AP, Dupret D, Tejero-Cantero A, Woolrich MW.
europmc-pmc4739513.description: The brain is capable of producing coordinated fast changing neural dynamics across multiple brain regions in order to adapt to rapidly changing environments. However, it is non-trivial to identify multiregion dynamics at fast sub-second time-scales in electrophysiological data....

pmc-10610007.title: The Development of a Smart Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Chemical Exchange Saturation Transfer Contrast Agent for the Imaging of Sulfatase Activity
pmc-10610007.creator: Ilse M Welleman, Friederike Reeβing, Hendrikus H Boersma, Rudi A J O Dierckx, Ben L Feringa, Wiktor Szymanski, Sara Pinto, Rafael Aroso
pmc-10610007.description: The molecular imaging of biomarkers plays an increasing role in medical diagnostics. In particular, the imaging of enzyme activity is a promising approach, as it enables the use of its inherent catalytic activity for the amplification of an imaging signal. The increased activity of a sulfatase enzyme has been observed in several types of cancers.

pmc-10611695.title: Five new Camillea (Xylariales) species described from French Guiana
pmc-10611695.creator: Jacques Fournier, Huei-Mei Hsieh, Christian Lechat, Yu-Ming Ju, Delphine Chaduli, Anne Favel
pmc-10611695.description: BackgroundThe genus Camillea was created in 1849 from collections made in French Guiana with eight species included. Numerous species assigned to Camillea were subsequently discovered, especially in the forests of the Amazon basin, but new discoveries have not been reported from French Guiana since 1849.

pmc-11399598.title: Exposure to nicotine pouch marketing and nicotine pouch experimentation among U.S. adults who use commercial tobacco
pmc-11399598.creator: Lilianna Phan, Kasra Zarei, Julia Chen-Sankey, Kiana Hacker, Aniruddh Ajith, Bambi Jewett, Kelvin Choi
pmc-11399598.description: Highlights•Almost half of U.S. adults who use commercial tobacco were aware of nicotine pouches through various marketing channels.•Awareness through each nicotine pouch marketing channel was associated with higher odds of nicotine pouch ever use.•Nicotine pouch marketing may be equally reaching varying demographic segments of U.S. adults who use commercial tobacco.

pmc-11422812.title: Responsive‐Hydrogel Aquabots
pmc-11422812.creator: Shipei Zhu, Huanqing Cui, Yi Pan, Derek Popple, Ganhua Xie, Zachary Fink, Jiale Han, Alex Zettl, Ho Cheung Shum, Thomas P Russell
pmc-11422812.description: It remains a challenge to produce soft robots that can mimic the responsive adaptability of living organisms. Rather than fabricating soft robots from bulk hydrogels,hydrogels are integrated into the interfacial assembly of aqueous two‐phase systems to generate ultra‐soft and elastic all‐aqueous aquabots that exhibit responsive adaptability, that can shrink on demand and have electrically conductive functions.

pmc-11523522.title: Signs and symptoms of serious illness in adults with acute abdominal pain presenting to ambulatory care: a systematic review
pmc-11523522.creator: Anouk Tans, Thomas Struyf, Rune Geboers, Toon Smeets, Yorick Asselbergh, Emmanuel Declerck, Luca Bloemen, Ann van den Bruel
pmc-11523522.description: BackgroundAcute abdominal pain is a common complaint, caused by a variety of conditions, ranging from acutely life-threatening to benign and self-limiting, with symptom overlap complicating diagnosis. Signs and symptoms may be valuable when assessing a patient to guide clinical work.

pmc-11691557.title: EXPLORING THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN INTERNET USE AND BELIEF IN CONSPIRACY THEORIES AMONG OLDER ADULTS IN JAPAN
pmc-11691557.creator: Masumi Takeuchi, Ai Fukuzawa, Tetsuro Kobayashi
pmc-11691557.description: The use of the internet among older adults in Japan has become increasingly prevalent, leading to both positive and negative effects, such as the association between internet use and belief in conspiracy theories (Toriumi, 2023). In Japan, it has been observed that older adults are more susceptible to conspiracy theories when exposed to extreme content, such as online videos.

pmc-11809947.title: The Usefulness of Vascularized Flap Craniotomy for Open-Wound Depressed Skull Fractures
pmc-11809947.creator: Yoichiro Nakahara, Jin Kikuchi, Yoshikuni Kotaki, Yusuke Otsu, Keisuke Sugi, Hidenobu Yoshitake, Tetsuya Negoto, Motohiro Morioka
pmc-11809947.description: BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE:Free bone flap craniotomy for open-wound depressed skull fractures poses a high risk of infection due to free bone fragments. This risk escalates in the presence of compound fractures with accompanying dural injuries. The primary objectives in managing depressed skull fractures include infection prevention and the correction of cosmetic deformities.

pmc-12650610.title: Systematic Review of Advanced Algorithms for Brain Mapping in Stereotactic Neurosurgery: Integration of fMRI and EEG Data
pmc-12650610.creator: Saleha Redžepi, Eldin Burazerović, Salim Redžepi, Emina Husović, Mirza Pojskić, Kymberly Young, Antonio Nicolato, Michele Longhi
pmc-12650610.description: Background: Advances in stereotactic neurosurgery rely on precise brain mapping, which allows the identification of functional regions for safer and more effective surgical interventions. The aim of this systematic review was to assess the effectiveness, challenges, and clinical applicability of algorithms used for multimodal data integration. Methodology: Databases were searched for studies published in the last 13 years.

pmc-12666141.title: The Health Survey of São Paulo – ISA-Physical Activity and Environment Longitudinal Study
pmc-12666141.creator: Alex Antonio Florindo, Bianca Mitie Onita, Inaian Pignatti Teixeira, Andreia Machado Miranda, Pedro Curi Hallal
pmc-12666141.description: PurposeThe main objective of the Health Survey of São Paulo or Inquérito de Saúde de São Paulo (ISA) in Portuguese, is to generate health indicators to support research and policy planning. The ISA-Physical Activity and Environment Longitudinal Study has the primary objective of examining built and social environmental determinants of leisure-time physical activity and active transportation.

pmc-12955177.title: Video laryngoscopy as a teaching tool in direct intubation in undergraduate medical education – a randomized controlled trial
pmc-12955177.creator: Daniel Uhing, Lina Vogt, Martin Klasen, Michelle Schmidt, Maurice Elissen, Nico Haehn, Sasa Sopka, Michael Tobias Schauwinhold
pmc-12955177.description: BackgroundDirect laryngoscopy (DL) is a crucial skill and continues to be indispensable. While the superiority of video laryngoscopy (VL) has been demonstrated regarding the rate of first attempt successful intubations, its application as a teaching tool for DL remains largely unexplored.

pmc-13048555.title: Understanding pneumococcal vaccine perceptions in seven countries: Findings from a cross-sectional survey
pmc-13048555.creator: Donovan B. Smith, Chelsea D’Silva, Scott Ratzan, Kenneth Rabin, Madison Fullerton, Jia Hu
pmc-13048555.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pneumococcal disease remains a major global cause of morbidity and mortality, yet vaccine uptake varies. Understanding how demographic, socioeconomic, and regional factors shape pneumococcal vaccine perceptions is essential for developing effective public health strategies. We conducted a stratified, cross-sectional survey of 7,000 adults across seven countries (Canada, Brazil, France, India, Nigeria, the United Kingdom, and the United States), with sampling structured by age, sex, income, and education. Perceptions of pneumococcal vaccine safety, efficacy, importance, and disease concern were assessed using Likert scales.

pmc-13283923.title: Association Between Alcohol Drinking Patterns and Multiple Metabolic Syndrome Components in Non‐Obese and Obese Individuals
pmc-13283923.creator: Ayako Kikuchi, Hisashi Yoshimoto, Takafumi Monma, Sakiko Ozawa, Momoko Tsuchida, Fumi Takeda
pmc-13283923.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimThis cross‐sectional study aimed to investigate the relationship between drinking patterns (combination of the frequency and amount of alcohol consumption) and the possession of multiple metabolic syndrome (MetS) components in non‐obese and obese individuals.MethodsData derived from medical examinations, specific health checkup questionnaires, and health insurance claims of 36 006 individuals aged 40–64 years from five health insurance associations affiliated with Japanese companies were analyzed.

pmc-13317675.title: Use of a Conversational Agent for Training Mental Health Professionals in Suicide Safety Planning: Pilot Feasibility and Acceptability Study
pmc-13317675.creator: Bénédicte Nobile, Zohar Elyoseph, Elia Gourguechonbuot, Josselin Guyodo, Jordi Garcia, Inbar Levkovich, Emilie Olie, Yuval Haber, Yossi Levi-Belz, Philippe Courtet
pmc-13317675.description: BackgroundSafety planning is recognized as one of the most effective interventions for reducing suicidal behaviors. The quality of safety plans strongly depends on professional training, and traditional methods, such as role-playing, are time-consuming and offer limited opportunities for repetition across diverse patient profiles. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may provide innovative solutions by offering accessible, flexible, and realistic training environments.
